chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man, from Abi al-Ward, who said:

I said to Abi Ja'far عليه السلام: Abu Zhabyan narrated to me that he saw 'Ali عليه السلام pour out water and then wipe over the khuffs. So he said: Abu Zhabyan lied. Has not the saying of 'Ali عليه السلام reached you: “Among you, the Book preceded the khuffs”? I said: Then is there any concession regarding them? He said: No, except from an enemy whom you fear, or snow by which you fear for your feet.
As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:

I said to him: Is there taqiyyah in wiping over the khuffs? He said: There are three matters in which I do not practice taqiyyah before anyone: drinking an intoxicant, wiping over the khuffs, and mut'ah of hajj.

So it does not contradict the first report, for several reasons. One of them is that he informed about himself that he does not practice taqiyyah in it before anyone, and it is possible that he only informed of that because he knew that he did not need that in which taqiyyah would be practiced in this matter; and he did not say: “You should not practice taqiyyah in it before anyone.” This is an interpretation mentioned by Zurarah ibn A'yan. The second is that he may have meant: I do not practice taqiyyah in it before anyone in the legal ruling by giving fatwa that wiping over them is not permitted, as opposed to the act itself, because that is known from his madhhab, so there is no basis for using taqiyyah in it. The third is that he may have meant: I do not practice taqiyyah in it before anyone when the fear does not reach fear for life or property; even if a slight hardship were to affect him, he would bear it. Taqiyyah in that is only permissible in the case of intense fear for life or property.

key_terms.الْخَوْفُ: fear, especially fear for life or property affecting legal concession
key_terms.الْفُتْيَا: the issuing of a legal ruling or juristic response
key_terms.الْكِتَابُ: the Qur'an, invoked here as taking precedence in determining the ruling
key_terms.تَقِيَّةٌ: dissimulation or precautionary concealment due to fear of harm
key_terms.رُخْصَةٌ: a legal concession or dispensation in cases of necessity
key_terms.مَسْحُ الْخُفَّيْنِ: wiping over leather socks or footwear in place of washing the feet in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: Is wiping over khuffs permitted in Shia fiqh, and can it ever be allowed due to taqiyyah or necessity?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling on wiping over khuffs during wudu (ablution) and rejects attributing its permissibility to Imam 'Ali عليه السلام. It also discusses the limited scope of taqiyyah in this issue and reconciles apparently differing reports through distinctions in circumstance, legal response, and levels of fear.
